06: Now let's add a brand, from start to finish.
Open The Switch, then Add a brand. It starts at Step 0, Check her.
Type her website.
Press Check her. It looks for duplicates, then runs the Screen.
Likely women-owned. Her own site names a woman founder who still owns it.
The steps unlock, but you still confirm her ownership in Owner and proof.
Press Start onboarding. It makes a hidden draft and opens step one.
Fetch has already run. Four products wait at step four.
Her description and logo are filled in for you. Always check them.
Add a one-line story, in our own words.
Your work saves as you type. Nothing is public until you publish.
Step two, Owner and proof. This is the most important step.
Her name, the evidence, and where she's based came from the check. Check each one.
Enter the share that's women-owned.
Date verified is the day you checked her ownership. Set to today is one click.
Add the founder's email, so she can be sent the certification invitation.
Step three, Shopping. Direct means no affiliate network yet.
Ships from is filled in from where she's based.
Step four, Products. Here are the four products Fetch found.
Each one gets a product type and a short why line. Ready means it can publish.
Under the table, choose her category. You can use the suggestion.
Step five, Review and publish. Everything is in one list.
The owner certification invitation goes out once the brand is live. If the button is greyed out for you, the owner sends it.
Publish checks everything one more time, then her products go live.
Her brand is live. In this demo, nothing really went live.
07: Service providers are women-owned businesses that offer a service. They're verified just like brands.
Open The Switch, then the Providers tab.
Add provider starts with Step 0, Check her, too.
Type the business name, then her city.
Choose her state. It tells her apart from others with the same name.
The kind of service is optional here. You can also add a new kind.
Add her website if she has one. Without it, one small search finds it by name and city.
Press Check her. It looks for duplicates, then runs the Screen.
Likely women-owned. It unlocks, but you still confirm her ownership.
Press Start onboarding. Her draft opens, filled in from the check.
List what she does.
Add her story, using only what she wrote or approved.
Ownership details are for admins only, and they're needed to publish.
Published stays off until everything is in. The line under it tells you what's missing.
Enter the owner's full name.
Then the day you checked.
The evidence link came from the check.
Now every requirement is met, so Published can be ticked.
Press Save.
And she's in the list, live and verified. In this demo, nothing really went live.
